# Incident Report: PCAP Traffic Analysis — 2026-01-31

**Evidence:** `2026-01-31-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (51,181 frames, 26.4 MB). No IDS/Suricata alert exports were provided alongside the capture — all findings below are derived directly from packet analysis.

## Victim Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.1.21.58** |
| MAC address | **00:21:5d:c8:0e:f2** (confirmed via ARP and DHCP request, consistent across the capture) |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-ES9F3ML** (NBNS `<00>`/`<20>`, DHCP option 12 hostname) |
| Windows domain | **win11office.com** (NetBIOS `WIN11OFFICE`), domain controller `WIN-LU4L24X3UB7.win11office.com` at 10.1.21.2 |
| Logged-in user | **gwyatt** (Kerberos `CNameString`, seen in AS-REQ/TGS traffic both from 10.1.21.58 and to the DC at 10.1.21.2) |

LAN scope: 10.1.21.0/24. 10.1.21.2 is the domain controller/gateway (heavy but entirely normal SMB2/DCERPC/SAMR/LSARPC/Kerberos/LDAP traffic — verified it never contacts any of the malicious external IPs below). No other local host generates suspicious traffic.

## Malware Family

**Attribution: behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS alerts were present in the evidence set).

The traffic shows a multi-stage delivery chain consistent with a commodity **Pay-Per-Install (PPI) loader / stealer distribution network using a JavaScript anti-analysis "fingerprinting gate"** ahead of the actual payload:

1. **~t=45s** — victim resolves `hiyter.com` (likely a redirect/landing page) followed almost immediately by `media.megafilehub4.lat` and `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (fake file-hosting-style domain names).
2. **~t=48s** — a 16 MB TLS transfer occurs to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` (104.21.46.67, Cloudflare-fronted, SNI hidden behind Encrypted Client Hello as `cloudflare-ech.com`) — the probable payload download. Content is TLS-encrypted, so the delivered file's name/hash could not be recovered from this capture.
3. **~t=90–122s** — the victim's browser(s) load `whooptm.cyou` and then repeatedly (24 short-lived TCP connections in a ~30-second window, ports 80 and 443) contact `whitepepper.su` (153.92.1.49). This is a browser-fingerprinting/anti-bot "gate": the served JavaScript collects `navigator.webdriver` (VM/automation detection), WebGL vendor/renderer, canvas fingerprint, WebRTC ICE candidates, AudioContext fingerprint, screen/hardware/locale data, and POSTs it to `/api/set_agent?id=<32-hex machine ID>&token=<40-hex session token>&agent=Chrome|Edge&act=log`. The page was executed once tagged `agent=Chrome` and once tagged `agent=Edge`, confirming both installed browsers were fingerprinted separately. Code contains a Russian-language comment (`// Преобразуем в URLSearchParams`).
4. **~t=122–128s** — further contact with `holiday-forever.cc` and `communicationfirewall-security.cc`, both with traffic skewed heavily outbound (upload > download), consistent with continued beaconing/exfiltration through the same gate infrastructure.

This pattern (fake download site → anti-sandbox/anti-bot browser fingerprinting gate with machine-ID/token tracking → repeated short-interval beaconing) matches TTPs commonly associated with 2025–2026 PPI loader/stealer campaigns (e.g., Lumma Stealer, Vidar, and PrivateLoader/HijackLoader-style gates). No single family name can be signature-confirmed from this evidence alone; this is the closest behavioral match.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 / gate endpoints (IP:port):**
- `153.92.1.49:443` and `153.92.1.49:80` — whitepepper.su (fingerprinting gate / beacon, 24 connections observed)
- `104.21.46.67:443` — arch.filemegahab4.sbs (payload delivery, 16 MB transferred; fronted by Cloudflare)
- `104.21.48.156:443` — media.megafilehub4.lat
- `62.72.32.156:443` — whooptm.cyou
- `80.97.160.24:443` — holiday-forever.cc
- `104.21.9.36:443` — communicationfirewall-security.cc
- `104.21.22.231:443` — hiyter.com

**Malicious/suspicious domains:**
- whitepepper.su
- arch.filemegahab4.sbs
- media.megafilehub4.lat
- whooptm.cyou
- holiday-forever.cc
- communicationfirewall-security.cc
- hiyter.com

**Malicious URLs (observed in cleartext HTTP):**
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Chrome&act=log`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge`
- `http://whitepepper.su/api/set_agent?id=3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C&token=842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b&description=&agent=Edge&act=log`

**Tracking identifiers (extracted from the gate URL):** machine/bot ID `3BF67EC05320C5729578BE4C0ADF174C`; session token `842e2802df0f0a06b4ed51f12f4387e761523b`.

**Transferred file names / hashes:** None available. The only files recoverable via HTTP object export were the gate's HTML/JS pages served over plaintext port 80 on `whitepepper.su` (fingerprinting script, SHA256 `a1ee2e3055dc4ce0d60eb6c2c8a655e705b3607bd33d65794e67adf22a2a0124` for the `agent=Chrome` variant, `8f97a4018d4b0675b9592660394cf5b73f1be2252e27aff64a8f160af9079f46` for `agent=Edge`) — these are gate infrastructure, not the delivered malware. The 16 MB payload transfer to `arch.filemegahab4.sbs` occurred entirely over TLS, so its filename and hash could not be extracted from this capture.

**Benign context (not indicators):** Traffic to Google, Microsoft (login.live.com, office.com, msftconnecttest.com), Bing/MSN, and Cloudflare CDN/insights endpoints is normal OS/browser telemetry and was excluded from the IOC list.
